instructions: Start the rice first. Rinse 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice, then add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water. Bring it to a boil over high heat, cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes. Leave the lid on and take the pot off the heat until you're ready to serve.

Pat the tofu dry and cut it into 1-inch cubes. Transfer them to a bowl and add 1 tbsp soy sauce, the Shaoxing wine, the ground cumin, the white pepper and the salt. Toss gently and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut the broccoli into small florets, thinly slice the onion and mince the garlic. In a small bowl, stir together 1 tbsp soy sauce, the sugar, 1 tsp of the cornstarch and 1/3 cup water.
Sprinkle 3 tbsp cornstarch over the tofu and toss gently until each cube has a dry, even coat.

Heat 3 tbsp of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until golden and crisp on most sides. Transfer to a plate.
Wipe out the pan and heat the last 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds. After about 20 seconds they'll sizzle and smell toasty. That's your cue for the onion.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, until it softens and starts to brown at the edges.
Add the broccoli and 2 tbsp water, cover and cook for 2 minutes, until it's bright green.
Take the lid off and add the garlic. Stir for 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce again and pour it in. Let it bubble for 1 minute, until it thickens a little.
Return the tofu to the pan, sprinkle on the Sichuan pepper and toss for 30 seconds.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve over the rice. Put the red pepper flakes in a small bowl on the table for anyone who wants it hot.
method_notes: No cumin tofu version had 20 or more ratings, so this is the fallback: Anna Ansari's Uyghur ziran doufu (Sous Chef) leads for the flavor, which is a cumin marinade, crisp fried tofu, toasted cumin seeds, onion and ground Sichuan pepper. I Spy Plum Pie and Vegan with Gusto add the broccoli and a cornstarch coating, which turn it into a full dinner. A short soy and water sauce is added so the plate has something spoonable, and the dried chilies are replaced by red pepper flakes on the table to keep the base mild.
